about: MCP servers and skills the panel's Tools tab recommends (wireface/harness_tools.py). Versions are pinned, as backends/claude.py pins Playwright's, so npx and uvx don't ask the registry on every start. Checked 2026-10-07. Wireface's own skills are in skills/.

mcp.title: Context7
mcp.description: Up-to-date documentation and code examples for thousands of libraries, looked up while the agent works.
mcp.why: Answers about the version you use, not the one the model remembers.
mcp.auth: No sign-in. A free key from context7.com raises the rate limit.

mcp.title: DeepWiki
mcp.description: Ask questions about any public GitHub repository and read its generated documentation.
mcp.why: "How does this library do X?" without cloning it.

mcp.title: Microsoft Learn
mcp.description: Searches and reads Microsoft's official documentation and code samples: Windows, .NET, Azure, PowerShell, Office.
mcp.why: Current answers about Windows and Microsoft tools, straight from the source.

mcp.title: Playwright browser
mcp.description: Drives a browser: opens pages, reads them, clicks, fills in forms and takes screenshots.
mcp.why: Lets the agent use and test web pages. Claude Code behind the face has it already (Wireface's browser).

needs.label: Node.js
needs.hint: Install Node.js first: it won't start without it.

needs.label: Chrome
needs.hint: Install Chrome first: it drives Chrome.

mcp.title: Chrome DevTools
mcp.description: Inspects a live Chrome: console messages, network requests, performance traces and screenshots.
mcp.why: For debugging web apps: the agent sees what DevTools shows you.

needs.label: Node.js 20.19 or later
needs.hint: Install Node.js first: it won't start without it.

needs.label: Chrome
needs.hint: Install Chrome first: it drives Chrome.

mcp.title: Memory
mcp.description: A small knowledge graph the agent can write to and read back: people, projects and facts to remember between conversations.
mcp.why: Things you tell it once (names, preferences, how a project fits together) are there next time.

needs.label: Node.js
needs.hint: Install Node.js first: it won't start without it.

mcp.auth: No sign-in. Kept in a file in your home folder (.mcp-memory).

mcp.title: Fetch
mcp.description: Fetches a web page and turns it into readable text.
mcp.why: Web reading for agents without it (Claude Code has its own WebFetch).

needs.label: uv
needs.hint: Install uv first: Fetch won't start without it.

mcp.auth: No sign-in. It can reach addresses on your own network, so use it with care.

mcp.title: GitHub
mcp.description: Issues, pull requests, code search, releases and Actions on GitHub.
mcp.why: "What's open on my repo?" and "open a pull request for this" by voice.

needs.label: GitHub token
needs.hint: Put a GitHub personal access token in the GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variable first: it can't sign in without one.

mcp.auth: The token is read from the environment variable, never written into the agent's config.

skills.title: Web app testing
skills.description: Tests a local web app with Playwright: starts its server, drives the pages, takes screenshots and reads the browser's logs.

skills.title: MCP builder
skills.description: Guides building a good MCP server in Python or TypeScript: designing its tools, then testing and evaluating them.

skills.title: Skill creator
skills.description: Helps write a new skill ("make a skill for how we do releases"), then test and improve it.

answer-on-screen.title: Answer on screen
answer-on-screen.description: Puts commands, code, links and long lists in a file on screen, and says the gist out loud.

dictation-notes.title: Dictation notes
dictation-notes.description: "Take a note", "add it to my to-do list": tidies what you dictate into dated notes, to-dos and drafts.

review-aloud.title: Review aloud
review-aloud.description: Reviews your changes, speaks the verdict and the top findings, and writes the full review to a file.

standup-briefing.title: Stand-up briefing
standup-briefing.description: A sixty-second spoken stand-up from the repository: done, in progress, blocked.

walk-me-through.title: Walk me through
walk-me-through.description: Guides you through a task on your own PC, one spoken step at a time, waiting between steps.
